elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: 12.4 "Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor"

elements.element: No field-of-use / territory restriction on Customer
elements.evidence: 12.3 "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory"; 12.4 now permits competing "in any territory"

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: 12.4 refers generically to "any product or service that competes with Vendor"; no named product

elements.element: Restriction limited to the term only (no post-term tail)
elements.evidence: 12.4 retains "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter"
No internal-development carve-out language appears in 12.4
No acquisition carve-out; "or acquire" appears only in the permission clause

reasons: The single operator swap of "shall not" to "may" in § 12.4 eliminates the non-compete and field-of-use restriction on Customer, meeting the preferred position.
Change is minimal: one short phrase replaced, no rewrite, no new exceptions, no boilerplate, and § 12.3's affirmative freedoms are left untouched.

Intent preserved: the residual permission in § 12.4 is merely declaratory and now aligns with § 12.3 rather than contradicting it; no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced. The surviving "twenty-four months thereafter" timeframe is harmless because it now qualifies a permission, not a prohibition.

Fallback elements (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, internal development and acquisition carve-outs) are unmet, but that is immaterial since the locked preferred level is satisfied and levels are not combined.
